title: Actionable customer requests + risk flags (May 2026)
content:
Audience: Product managers (Hosted API, Dedicated), Product Ops, Eng triage leads
Date: 2026-05-10 (last updated 2026-05-14)
Prepared by: Sofia Ramirez (CS)
Purpose: Condense recent customer feedback into a prioritized, actionable list plus operational risk flags that should influence short-term roadmaps and support tickets. This is intentionally pragmatic — focuses on requests we can scope or mitigate in the next 1–3 quarters.

Executive summary:
- Collected ~72 discrete asks from enterprise pilots, support logs, and solutioning calls in April–May.
- Four recurring high-impact themes: predictable latency across long-context workloads; improved model fallback behavior; simpler token/cost forecasting for customers on Dedicated; and structured output/validation hooks for tool-calling.
- Proposed immediate actions: 3 quick product fixes (low dev cost), 2 guided docs/recipes (doc + example configs), and 3 roadmap candidates to evaluate for Q3 planning.

Key metrics / signal context:
- Source mix: 40% enterprise pilots (Tier 1–2), 35% support tickets, 25% AE/SE discovery chats.
- Top tags applied during triage: latency-variance (27 mentions), fallback-behavior (23), billing-clarity (18), structured-output (15).
- Notable customers: FinRegBank (sensitive-regs, on Dedicated), TravelMate (PLG + high concurrency), EduSys (on Hosted API, long-context transcripts).

Actionable requests (prioritized):
1) Deterministic latency tiering for long-context sessions
   - Request: Customers want SLO-like guarantees or clearer expectations when using >16k token windows. They reported unpredictable tail latency spikes during transcription stitching.
   - Frequency: High (17 distinct customers)
   - Impact: High (affects transactional UX and SLAs)
   - Suggested owner: eng-serving-runtime + product-hosted-api
   - Suggested next step: Add a published latency profile matrix for model variants and sequence lengths; short-term doc + SDK helper to detect and warn when request size crosses thresholds.
   - Estimated effort: M

2) Configurable model fallback with labeled degradation modes
   - Request: When capacity or latency triggers fallback, customers want explicit labeling and predictable quality degradation (e.g., "quantized-fast" vs "standard-approx").
   - Frequency: Medium (12 customers + SRE incidents)
   - Impact: High for reliability-sensitive customers
   - Suggested owner: platform-engineering + product-dedicated
   - Proposed mitigation: Expose fallback policy options in Console (prefer-latency / prefer-quality / notify-and-fallback) and emit structured events to webhooks/logs.
   - Estimated effort: L (UI + backend coordination)

3) Token/cost forecast tool for Dedicated customers
   - Request: Need a simple forecast that maps expected token volumes and batching behavior to monthly cost estimates (including autoscale/burst scenarios).
   - Frequency: Medium-high (20 mentions across sales + CS conversations)
   - Impact: Medium-high on committed capacity decisions
   - Suggested owner: product-dedicated + finance-and-legal
   - Quick win: Spreadsheet template and Console report showing projected cost under three traffic profiles (steady, diurnal, burst).
   - Estimated effort: S

4) Structured-output validation hooks and retry semantics for tool-calls
   - Request: Customers building orchestration layers want first-class validation hooks so malformed tool outputs can trigger deterministic retries or alternative flows.
   - Frequency: Medium (esp. automation and SE teams)
   - Impact: Medium
   - Suggested owner: developer-experience + product-hosted-api
   - Proposed near-term: Cookbook + sample SDK wrappers implementing validation + retry policy.

5) Better observability for per-route token breakdowns in Hosted API
   - Request: More granular, per-route insights: token origin (prompt/context/cache/response) and per-request anomaly flags.
   - Frequency: Lower but high signal (5 enterprise customers asked explicitly)
   - Impact: Medium (debugging + cost optimisation)
   - Suggested owner: observability + console-and-rollouts
   - Estimated effort: M

Quick wins (can be shipped within 2–6 weeks):
- Publish "Latency by sequence length" public doc with sample data for top 5 models (owner: eng-serving-runtime + devx).
- Console: add a checkbox to email or webhook when fallback happens (owner: console-and-rollouts).
- Dedicated: provide a ready-made cost-forecast spreadsheet + guide for AEs to use during negotiations (owner: product-dedicated).

Operational risk flags (require immediate attention / mitigation):
- Miscommunication risk: Several customers self-remediated by switching to higher-cost model variants without notifying support — leads to billing surprises and churn risk. Mitigation: billing alert email + Console banner when estimated monthly spend crosses customer-specific threshold. (owner: finance-and-legal + console)

- Edge-case regression risk: A recent kernel selection change (internal PR referenced in linked_artifacts) can increase latency for small-batch small-seq traffic. We saw 3 customers report regression post-deploy. Action: roll-forward quick patch and add canary across low-latency customers. (owner: serving-runtime + sre)

- Compliance/workflow risk: FinRegBank asked for deterministic model hashing for audit trails (proof of output origin). This is likely a Q3 backlog item but we should acknowledge and scope with legal/security now. (owner: security-and-compliance + private-deployments)

Customer quotes (verbatim snippets used during triage):
- "We had a transcript at 45k tokens and the tail latency made the user session time out — we lost revenue on a booking flow." — TravelMate SE
- "When fallback kicked in it silently downgraded; our checks didn't trigger because there was no structured flag." — Internal engineering lead, EduSys
- "We need something to show our finance team what the Dedicated commit will actually cost under real patterns." — FinRegBank procurement

Suggested roadmap moves for Q3 planning (for PM discussion):
- Q3 candidate A: Fallback policy surface + structured event emission (High impact, cross-team).
- Q3 candidate B: Deterministic latency profiles + SDK warnings for large contexts (High impact, lower infra risk).
- Q3 candidate C: Observability upgrade for token-level breakdowns (Medium impact, supports sales).

Immediate next steps (owners + dates):
- 2026-05-18: Eng-serving-runtime to publish preliminary latency-by-length datasets (owner: Priya Menon)
- 2026-05-21: Console team to add fallback notification checkbox and email webhook (owner: Liam O'Neill)
- 2026-05-25: CS to distribute cost-forecast spreadsheet to AEs and collect 10 sample customer inputs for tuning (owner: Sofia Ramirez)
- 2026-06-01: Cross-functional sync to triage roadmap candidates and map required effort (invite: product-hosted-api, product-dedicated, serving-runtime, observability, security).

Appendix A — sample ticket list (high-signal):
- RDW-4823: "Latency spike with 48k token transcript" (TravelMate)
- RDW-4910: "Fallback behavior silently downgraded model" (EduSys)
- RDW-4992: "Dedicated cost predictability request" (FinRegBank)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc pulls from CS triage tags and a small manual read of support threads — it's intentionally operational. Please add comments inline in Confluence page RDW-cs-monthly-2026-05 (linked above) if you disagree with prioritization.

End of doc.
